title: Pool Length and a Tennis Line
bigQuestion: How did a swim in open water and a game on a lawn become races and matches with measured rooms?

story.title: A Rope on the Water
story.kicker: Before a school swim meet, a rope of floats is stretched across the water, wall to wall.
paragraphs: It is early morning at a school pool in Illinois. The water is flat and still. A worker pulls a long rope of plastic floats from one wall to the far wall. Then another, and another. Soon the pool is split into lanes.

The pool is 25 yards long. A dark line on the bottom runs down the middle of each lane. At each end, a wall waits for swimmers to touch. The same length is used by many school pools across the United States.
Outside, beyond the parking lot, are the tennis courts. White lines mark a long rectangle. A net hangs across the middle. The lines look the same as lines on courts in other states and countries.

Neither room looked like this 150 years ago. Swimmers raced in rivers, lakes and the sea. Tennis was first played on grass, with a court shaped like an hourglass. Rope and paint came from people agreeing on a shared plan.
story.think: What do a floating rope and a painted tennis line have in common?

lessons.title: Races in Open Water
lessons.mainIdea: The first modern Olympic swimming races were held in open water; a built pool came in 1908.
reading: At the first modern Olympics in Athens in 1896, swimmers raced in the sea. The races were held in a bay near the port of Piraeus. The water was cold and rough. There were no walls and no lanes.

At the 1900 Paris Games, swimmers raced in the river Seine. The river's current pushed them along. That made times faster than in still water. Those times could not be compared with times from other places.

For the 1908 London Games, a *pool* was built inside the main stadium. It was 100 meters long. For the first time, Olympic swimmers raced in a still, measured tank. Later Games used built pools every time.

words.d: a sea, lake or river, not a built pool
a tank of water built to a measured size
water moving in one direction, as in a river

look.title: Three Olympic Swims

check.why: The 1896 races were held in a bay near Piraeus.

check.why: London built a 100-meter pool inside its stadium for 1908.

lessons.title: Short Course and Long Course
lessons.mainIdea: Swimming records are kept separately for short-course pools and 50-meter long-course pools.
reading: In 1908, swimming leaders from several countries met in London. They formed FINA, a world body for swimming. It wrote rules and kept world records. In 2022, FINA renamed itself *World Aquatics*.
Today the Olympics use a 50-meter pool. Swimmers call this *long course*. A 25-meter pool is called *short course*. World Aquatics keeps a separate record list for each length.

Many U.S. high school pools are 25 yards long. That is shorter than 25 meters. So a time from a yard pool cannot be compared straight to a time from a meter pool. Swim records always say which pool was used.

words.d: a 50-meter pool, the size used at the Olympics
a 25-meter pool, or in the United States often a 25-yard pool
the world swimming body, founded in 1908 as FINA and renamed in 2022

check.why: The world swimming body was called FINA from 1908 until 2022.

check.q: Why do swim records say which pool was used?
check.why: Times from different pool lengths cannot be compared straight.

lessons.title: Lane Lines and Walls
lessons.mainIdea: Floating lane lines and painted lines on the pool floor give each swimmer a fair, marked path.
reading: A *lane line* is a rope strung with floats. It runs from one end wall to the other. It marks where one swimmer's lane ends and the next begins. Rule books set how many lanes a race pool has.

Early lane lines were simple ropes with cork floats. Later designs used plastic discs that spin in the water. These discs break up waves. So a swimmer in one lane is less bothered by splashing next door.
Rule books also call for a dark line on the floor down each lane. At each end, a *touchpad* can sit on the wall. When a swimmer touches it, the clock stops. This is how pools use automatic timing.

words.d: a floating rope that marks the edge of a swimming lane
a panel on a pool wall that stops the clock when touched

lessons.title: Real Tennis Indoors
lessons.mainIdea: Long before lawn tennis, people played an older game, now called real tennis, in walled indoor courts.
reading: In France in the Middle Ages, people played a ball game called *jeu de paume*. The name means game of the palm. At first, players hit the ball with their hands. Later they used rackets.

The game moved into large walled rooms. In English it became known as tennis. Today it is called *real tennis*, to tell it apart from lawn tennis. King Henry VIII had a court built at Hampton Court Palace near London.
Real tennis courts were costly. Mostly kings, nobles and rich men played. Each court was a bit different in size and shape. That made it hard to set one plan everyone could share.

words.d: French for game of the palm; an old ball game that became real tennis
the older indoor game of tennis played in walled courts

lessons.title: Wingfield's Boxed Game
lessons.mainIdea: Walter Clopton Wingfield introduced a lawn tennis game in 1873 and patented it in 1874.
reading: Walter Clopton Wingfield was a British army officer. In 1873 he introduced an outdoor game for lawns. In 1874 he took out a *patent* on it. He gave it a Greek name, *Sphairistikè*, meaning ball game.

Wingfield sold the game in a box. It held rackets, balls, a net, poles and a printed rule book. Buyers marked out the court on their own grass. His court was wider at the ends and narrow at the net, like an hourglass.

The boxed set sold well in Britain and beyond. Lawn tennis spread to gardens, clubs and parks. Players soon changed his rules and his court shape. But his box helped many people start playing the same game.

words.d: a government paper that names who invented something
the Greek name Wingfield gave his lawn tennis game
the British officer who introduced lawn tennis in 1873 and patented it in 1874

check.why: He took out his patent in 1874, a year after he introduced the game.

check.q: What shape was Wingfield's first court?
check.why: His court was wider at the ends and narrow at the net.

lessons.title: Wimbledon, 1877
lessons.mainIdea: The first Wimbledon tournament in 1877 used a rectangle court that became the standard.
reading: The All England Croquet Club was in Wimbledon, near London. In 1875 it added lawn tennis. In 1877 it held a lawn tennis championship. This was the first *Wimbledon*.
For that event, the club wrote its own rules. It dropped the hourglass shape. The singles court became a rectangle 78 feet long and 27 feet wide. That shape is still used today.
Twenty-two men entered the first championship. Spencer Gore won. Women were not included at first. Wimbledon added a women's singles event in 1884, and Maud Watson won it.

words.d: the tennis championship of the All England Club, first held in 1877
a match with one player on each side

check.q: Who won the first Wimbledon in 1877?
check.why: Spencer Gore won the first Wimbledon men's singles.

check.q: What shape did the 1877 Wimbledon court take?
check.why: The club's 1877 rules used a rectangle court.

check.q: When did Wimbledon add a women's singles event?
check.why: Women's singles began at Wimbledon in 1884.

lessons.title: IHSA Swimming Titles
lessons.mainIdea: The IHSA crowned its first boys swimming champions in 1932 and its first girls swimming champions in 1975.
reading: A state swim meet needs pools that are the same length. It also needs rules for timing and lanes. The IHSA held its first boys state swimming and diving meet in 1932.

For more than 40 years, only boys had a state swim meet in Illinois. Girls' swimming and diving got its own IHSA state series in 1975. Many girls had swum before then, but they had no state title to race for.
School pools are costly to build, heat and staff. Some Illinois schools have no pool at all. Their swimmers may practice in a park district pool or join a team from a nearby school.

words.d: an event where athletes jump from a board into the water; paired with swimming in IHSA meets
the set of IHSA meets or games that leads to a state champion

check.why: The first IHSA boys state swim meet was in 1932.

lessons.title: IHSA Tennis Titles
lessons.mainIdea: The IHSA crowned its first boys tennis champion in 1912 and its first girls tennis champion in 1972.
reading: Tennis is one of the oldest IHSA state series. The first boys tennis champion was crowned in 1912. That was 35 years after the first Wimbledon. School courts used the same rectangle as the 1877 rules.

Girls tennis waited 60 more years. The IHSA held its first girls tennis state series in 1972. That same year, Congress passed *Title IX*. This federal law says schools that get U.S. money cannot shut people out because of sex.
IHSA tennis and swimming records list each year's champions. Reading down the list shows who could play, and when. The empty years before 1972 and 1975 are part of that history too.

words.d: a 1972 federal law saying schools that get U.S. money cannot shut people out because of sex
an official list of past champions and results
